short: Total Hoare triples and probability-one termination

lean.name: Triple
lean.plain: The expectation inequality in a Hoare triple
lean.annotation: The right-hand side uses `(interp c).toStateFun Δ` as returned. If a program aborts on a branch of mass $1/2$ and preserves the other half, the output trace is $1/2$. Even the identity postcondition has expectation only $1/2$ on that output, so a precondition of expectation one cannot establish this triple.

lean.name: expect_top
lean.plain: Total trace from the identity assertion
lean.annotation: By `expect_top`, the expectation of $\top$ on the output is its trace. A total triple with $\top$ on both sides therefore requires the program to preserve the input trace. On a trace-one input, this gives probability-one termination.

statements.section: Appendix A Formal Quantum Computation Library

lean.name: Triple
lean.plain: The expectation inequality in a Hoare triple
lean.annotation: The right-hand side of `Triple` is bounded above by the output trace, which is at most one. A precondition with expectation one therefore forces both the output trace and the postcondition expectation to be one. On such an input the program terminates and satisfies the postcondition with probability one.

statements.markdown: Correctness in this work is expressed through total Hoare triples
